The enhanced ACT Math test (from September 2025) is 45 multiple-choice questions in 50 minutes — about 67 seconds each — and a calculator is allowed throughout. 41 questions are scored; 4 are unscored field-test items you can't identify, so answer every one. Questions run roughly easy to hard, drawing on everything from pre-algebra to trigonometry.

figure.title: ACT 20-20-20 Pacing Curve: Cumulative Minutes vs Question Number

caption.en: The 20-20-20 ACT pacing rule banks 5 minutes on the first 20 questions to spend on the hardest final 20 questions.

ariaLabel.en: ACT Pacing Curve Explorer across 60 questions

body.en: Four answer choices per question (the enhanced ACT dropped the fifth). There is no formula sheet, so the key formulas must be memorized. The content spans number & quantity, algebra, functions, geometry, and statistics & probability.
Don't linger — flag a hard item and move on so easy points aren't lost. Backsolve from the answer choices, and plug in convenient numbers for variables when a question is abstract.

• Questions 1–15 (Easy): Spend ~40 seconds per question (10 minutes total). Bank time early while building confidence.
  • Questions 16–30 (Medium): Spend ~65 seconds per question (16 minutes total). Watch for multi-step algebra and word problems.
  • Questions 31–45 (Hard): Spend ~85 seconds per question (21 minutes total). These feature advanced geometry, trigonometry, and novel combinations.
  • Final 3 Minutes: Check flagged items and ensure EVERY single question has a bubbled answer!

• No Negative Marking: There is absolutely no penalty for wrong answers on the ACT. An unanswered question is guaranteed 0 points; an educated guess gives a 25% to 50% chance of a point.
  • 4-Choice Format: Enhanced ACT has 4 options (A, B, C, D) instead of 5, boosting blind guessing accuracy from 20% to 25%. Eliminating just one obvious wrong answer raises your odds to 33.3%, and eliminating two gives a 50% coin-flip.
  • Letter of the Day: If running out of time on the last 3–4 questions, pick one consistent letter (e.g., C) for all remaining items rather than alternating randomly.

label.en: Worked Example 0.A — Back-Solving from the Middle Choice (C / H)

body.en:
When an ACT algebra word problem offers five numerical choices in ascending order \((A\text{ to }E)\), testing choice \(C\) first eliminates half the remaining choices immediately if \(C\) is too small or too large.

Example: If \(\sqrt{2x + 7} = x - 4\), choices are \(A)\;1, B)\;5, C)\;9, D)\;11, E)\;15\).
Test \(C (x=9)\): \(\sqrt{2(9)+7} = \sqrt{25} = 5\), and \(9 - 4 = 5\). Matches immediately!

label.en: Worked Example 0.B — Plugging In Convenient Numbers for Variables

body.en: If \(x\) is an odd integer, which expression must be an even integer? Choose \(x = 3\) and evaluate each choice in seconds rather than expanding algebraic identities.

label.en: Worked Example 0.C — Allocating Time Across Multi-Question Data Sets

body.en: Every ACT Math section contains a 3-question stem sharing a table or diagram (usually around Q32–Q34). Spend 20 seconds reading the stem headings once, then solve all 3 questions in 2.5 minutes total.

label.en: Worked Example 0.D — Eliminating Scale-Trap Distractors in Late Geometry

body.en: On Q50–Q60, when a diagram asks for a length in a composite figure with legs \(6\) and \(8\), eliminate any choice equal to \(6+8=14\) and check the Pythagorean hypotenuse \(\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\).

question.en: On the enhanced ACT Math test (45 questions in 50 minutes), a student allocates 10 minutes to the first 15 questions and 16 minutes to questions 16 through 30. How many seconds per question remain for the final 15 questions, assuming 3 minutes are reserved at the end to check answers?

solution.en: \(\text{Time spent so far} = 10 + 16 = 26\text{ minutes}\). Leaving 3 minutes for review leaves \(50 - 26 - 3 = 21\text{ minutes}\) for the final 15 questions. \(\text{Time per question} = \frac{21 \times 60\text{ seconds}}{15\text{ questions}} = \frac{1260}{15} = 84\text{ seconds per question}\).

question.en: Under the 20-20-20 pacing strategy, how many minutes should remain on the 60-minute clock when you finish Question 20?

solution.en: You spend 15 minutes on Questions 1–20, leaving \(60 - 15 = \mathbf{45\text{ minutes}}\) remaining.

question.en: Does the ACT Math test penalize wrong guesses, or should every single question be answered before time expires?

solution.en: There is no guessing penalty on the ACT; raw score equals the count of correct answers out of 60. Never leave a bubble blank.

question.en: Why should you test Choice C (or H) first when back-solving numerical answer choices on the ACT?

solution.en: ACT numerical choices are ordered from least to greatest (or greatest to least). Testing the middle choice tells you whether to move higher or lower, requiring at most 2 tests.
